question: What did Britain use to replace enslaved labour on its sugar colonies after 1834?
answer: Indentured Indians. In 1834 Britain chose Mauritius for what it called the great experiment: workers bound by contract for years instead of owned. Between 1834 and 1920 almost half a million landed at one depot in Port Louis, the Aapravasi Ghat; others were shipped on to the Caribbean and Africa.
move: When one system of labour is abolished, look at what replaced it.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Aapravasi Ghat
